clue.text: Deer says drunkenly "What a shame!"

indicators.note: speech that is slurred by drink blurs the phrase into something said differently, so the letters follow the slurred sound

parts.note: the exclamation 'what a shame!' means 'what a pity!'

explanation.surface: A deer exclaims tipsily that something is a pity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'says drunkenly' asks you to slur 'what a pity' until it comes out as the name of the deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The wapiti is the large North American elk, a species of deer.

clue.text: Bitter herb damaging furniture when inverted

indicators.note: inverted turns the word end over end, so its two halves swap places

parts.note: woodworm are beetle larvae that bore into and damage wooden furniture

explanation.surface: A bitter plant harms the furniture when turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Wormwood is a bitter aromatic plant used in absinthe.

clue.text: Fencing assistant to the Queen, they say

indicators.note: 'they say' marks speech, so the phrase heard aloud gives the answer

parts.note: an aide working at the Queen's palace is a palace aide

explanation.surface: A royal attendant reportedly takes up swordplay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fencing' suggests swordplay but means a fence of stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence made of pointed wooden stakes, so fencing.

clue.text: Authentic Shakespeare, approved for trial

parts.note: authentic means true
Bill is the familiar name of William Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A genuine Shakespeare text is approved for testing.
explanation.walkthrough: A true bill was a grand jury's endorsement of an indictment, sending the case to trial.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a bill of indictment found sound by a grand jury is passed for trial.

clue.text: I was critical about nothing on my own

indicators.note: one piece is placed around another, so the critical verb wraps the zero

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly, so 'was critical' is slated
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone admits they were critical of something worthless, standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on your own is being apart from others, cut off and alone.

clue.text: Outstanding performer gets money - £1,000 for everyone entering — it goes up at the off

definitions.text: it goes up at the off

parts.note: a star is an outstanding performer
tin is old slang for money
a grand, £1,000, is G
the gate is the number of spectators admitted to an event

explanation.surface: A star performer earns a grand from the crowd at the start of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the off' is racing talk for the start; the barrier lifts as the horses break.
explanation.definitionFit: A starting gate is the barrier raised to release racehorses at the start.

clue.text: Fire beginning to burn out — do nothing

indicators.note: 'out' means taken away, so a letter leaves the fire word

parts.note: a blaze is a fire

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Let the fire burn itself out while you sit idle.
explanation.definitionFit: To laze is to idle, lounging about doing nothing.

clue.text: Hat for one who drinks about a quarter of a pint

indicators.note: about means around, so the drinker surrounds the letter

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker

indicators.note: a quarter of a four-letter word is one letter, here its first

explanation.surface: A drinker with a hat nurses a small measure of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: topper is the informal name for a tall silk top hat worn with formal dress.

clue.text: Give what happened at the high table?

definitions.meaning: to give money or goods to a cause

definitions.text: what happened at the high table?
definitions.meaning: at a college high table the dons dine

explanation.surface: A college fellow gives, at a formal dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: High table is where the senior members of an Oxford or Cambridge college, the dons, eat: so a don ate.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give something, especially to charity.

clue.text: Arrive with DIY cigarette

definitions.meaning: a hand-rolled cigarette made by the smoker from loose tobacco

explanation.surface: Someone turns up carrying a home-rolled smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to arrive casually and a cigarette you roll yourself.

clue.text: Graduate raced without vigour for paste

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate degree

indicators.note: here 'without' means outside, so one word goes round the other rather than lacking it

parts.note: raced means ran
zip is energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A graduate dashed about, lacking energy, in search of glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking vigour', but here it is the old sense 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marzipan is a sweet almond paste used on cakes.

clue.text: Bold mortal to venture all his money

indicators.note: to venture is to take a chance, so the letters are risked in a new order

explanation.surface: A brave human gambles all his cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Betting your bottom dollar is staking the last of your money.
explanation.definitionFit: Your bottom dollar is the last of your money, all that you have.

clue.text: From Aix to Ghent (more or less) news threw tots out

definitions.text: From Aix to Ghent (more or less)

indicators.note: 'out' means put out of order, so the letters of the three words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tale of riders carrying news from one Flemish city to another, while children get thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning's poem 'How They Brought the Good News from Ghent to Aix' prompts the reversed journey: Ghent lies roughly in this direction from Aix (Aachen).
explanation.definitionFit: A compass bearing that roughly describes the direction you travel from Aachen to Ghent.

clue.text: See 12
See 12
Theatreland's cause of flurry with beheading in Hamlet

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the prince's nationality

parts.note: Hamlet was a Dane, Prince of Denmark

indicators.note: the cause of something stirs it up, so these letters are rearranged
beheading removes the first letter

explanation.surface: London theatreland is stirred up by a decapitation in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' is not a small village but the Prince of Denmark; 'cause of' asks for the beheaded flurry (LURRY) to be stirred up into RURYL.
explanation.definitionFit: Drury Lane in London is home to the Theatre Royal and stands for the theatre district.

clue.text: Turn to God?

parts.note: suggests religious conversion, but means change someone into a god

explanation.definitionFit: To deify is to make a god of someone, turning them into one.

clue.text: Bonnie prince's dad deplored rent adjustment

indicators.note: an adjustment rearranges, so the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: A father complains that his rent has been changed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonnie Prince Charlie was the Young Pretender to the British throne; his father James Stuart was the Old one.
explanation.definitionFit: James Francis Edward Stuart, the Jacobite claimant called the Old Pretender, was father of Bonnie Prince Charlie.

clue.text: This girl is a man that's lost it

indicators.note: something lost has gone, so the letters of the little word leave the phrase

parts.note: the girl's name running unbroken through these words is a coincidence; the setter's device is taking I and T out, as 'lost it' says

explanation.surface: Someone describes a man who has lost his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost it' reads as losing one's temper; take I and T from 'is a man that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Samantha is a girl's name.

clue.text: Most of the Sitwells are around, so to speak

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word goes outside the other
most of a word leaves its tail off, so the end letters go

explanation.surface: Most of the famous literary Sitwell family are present.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sitwells (Edith, Osbert, Sacheverell) were an English literary family; 'Most of' trims the name to SITWE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'as it were' qualifies a figure of speech, much like 'so to speak'.

clue.text: Dairy product (product of years) brother is pursuing

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so the brother and 'is' come after the earlier pieces

parts.note: something that is the product of a thing comes from it
years add up to age
Fra is the title of an Italian friar, a brother, as in Fra Angelico

explanation.surface: A cheese made over the years is chased by a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: Fromage frais is a soft fresh cheese, a dairy food.

clue.text: Have another pull to annoy the bull

definitions.meaning: a scarlet cloth waved at a bull is said to enrage it

explanation.surface: Someone tugs again to provoke a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-drag it means pull again; as two words it is the cloth that provokes a bull.

clue.text: Does wrong circulating copper currency

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the metal
done wrong means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Bad does pass copper coins around.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was the currency of Portugal before the euro.

clue.text: Creation of the States (USA) with love from Ghent to Aix

indicators.note: a creation made out of these words is a new arrangement of their letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: The founding of the United States, sent with affection along Browning's famous ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The companion to 12: Browning's riders went from Ghent to Aix (Aachen), roughly this direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass bearing roughly matching the route from Ghent in Belgium to Aachen in Germany.

Rue changing fur that could have been worn again

definitions.text: that could have been worn again

indicators.note: changing alters the order, so the letters of rue are rearranged

parts.note: sable is a prized fur

explanation.surface: Someone regrets swapping a fur coat that might have been worn another time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reusable can be used a second time, here a garment put on again.

clue.text: Bond's grasping opt-out -on his points?

indicators.note: grasping means holding inside, so the bond wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a bond is a tie

indicators.note: 'out' means disordered, so the letters of opt are mixed up

explanation.surface: James Bond clutches an escape clause, dancing like a ballerina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007; 'opt-out' splits into fodder and its indicator 'out', the jumble being PTO. To be on tiptoe is to be on your points, like a ballet dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing on the points of your toes, as a ballet dancer does, is being on tiptoe.

clue.text: Piano hire will be appreciated

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
to lease is to hire

explanation.surface: A note saying that renting a piano would be welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding the polite word to a request signals that compliance will be gratefully received.
